# The same invoice as `fx_usd_invoice_settled_exactly_by_retarget.txt`, edited
# — the description differs, so the import unposts and rebuilds it — asking for
# whatever credit the customer has and naming no payment of its own.
#
# No payment block on purpose. With one, the settlement is re-attached before
# any credit is looked for and there is nothing left to apply; without one, the
# lot is open when `auto_apply_credit: true` hands the choice to GnuCash, which
# searches for open, owner-attached lots naming nothing. That is exactly what
# this invoice's own unpost left a moment earlier, so the engine can hand the
# invoice back the settlement it already had, with nothing in the file asking
# for it. Put back is not spent: called a credit applied, the export loses the
# account and the date the bank paid on.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.

invoice "INV-USD-RETARGET"
	customer_id: "C-US"
	currency: USD
	date_opened: 2026-01-05
	auto_apply_credit: true
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-05
		description: "Consulting, revised"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-01-05
		due: 2026-02-05
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
		memo: "Invoice INV-USD-RETARGET"
		accumulate: true
